We've got a bit of a weird situation right now which has happened a few times now but I wanted to note it. Just recently https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/pull/14964 landed which I believe invalidated all prior ISLE caches I assume due to structural changes since it's ISLE-related. This means that PR, expectedly, took ~4h in the merge queue to run full verification.

The problem though is that every PR right now is going to take 4h to do a full verification as well. We've got a 13-deep merge queue at the moment where everything active is doing ISLE verification. I believe the reason for this is that github caches for the merge queue restore from main, but the main cache is only populated once a night when a manual run is done on main.

I'm not really sure of a great fix for this myself other than maybe more aggressively pulling from the dev release as opposed to github caches. I've long not really liked github caches and how they're affine to branches since it's kind of never what we actually want for this very reason...

the main cache is only populated once a night when a manual run is done on main.

ah, shoot, that explains it -- privately we were puzzling over why the cache wasn't hitting...

This is a tricky one. This kind of nondeterminism/brittleness is what I was worried about when proposing to check in the cache into git instead; of course there are other good reasons we didn't do that (trust root, non-invasiveness, merge conflicts). I worry that a best-effort "slurp up the cache from [all the sources] to try to get latest runs" may still be brittle in some cases. But maybe that's the best we can do...
I'll see if I can put together a PR to do that. In the meantime if we want to unblock, I'm happy to comment out the isle-veri job and jump the queue with that if folks agree
nah it's not the end of the world really, it just means that everything will build up a big queue and land all at once after we all go to sleep
ideally what I want, for other reasons too, is to get off of github actions' cache onto something manual like azure or aws
With the hashing we have we basically have no need for branch-affine caches
I want any cache-write from any merge queue entry to get visible to all the others immediately
right, does our GitHub/Microsoft relationship give us any Azure bucket credits or anything? it wouldn't be that hard to do a content-addressed thing
Not that I know of
I want to turn this on for sccache too as well
this seems like a good question for the BA TSC/board -- if BA has budget for some cloud storage, we could do Good Things (cc @Oscar Spencer @Till Schneidereit)
In the meantime though I mostly just wanted to flag the issue here, the ISLE bits aren't changing that much so this doesn't happen like every day
we already discussed this, and do indeed have the budget. Setting it up turned out to be the more difficult thing
ah, interesting
to the extent that it's not really feasible, or could someone (say, one of us) spend some time to look into it more?
the latter. I started looking into it, and then was eaten by a grue ran into SSO auth issues when trying to connect our azure marketplace account to something that supports billing, or somesuch thing
that sounds like a fairly... nightmarish... nightmare, but if there's a way I can help (with what access I have anyway), let me know

I wonder if the easiest thing to do might be to try it out with some account and get things hooked up with a BA credit card it if works. I'd be happy to pay for a month of it myself, but I also don't have the bandwidth to do the setting up :confused:

I mean, I have AWS already with autobilling (all my personal DNS+web+...), and S3 is extremely cheap, so I'm happy to play with it on a personal access token scoped to one bucket, as long as the endgame is "BA provides an IAM access token for production S3"

I don't know anything about secrets management in GitHub CI but I can figure that part out...
if you're willing to do that, that I'll gladly commit to fighting the grue once it's time to hook up billing
note that with AWS egress costs might be a concern

my rough assumption for the architecture is that we'd have a bucket somewhere which is world-readable and readable without a token (e.g. PRs which don't get secrets can get cache hits), and then if egress costs are a problem we'd put a CDN in front of it

looking at the pricing table (https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/) the other thing that might bite is us per-request costs, unless we batch somehow -- a GET per SMT query could add up at 1k req for a half-cent (with a few thousand requests per run)
so maybe we need to invent the equivalent of git packfiles or something
nono we'd still have that be just "one file"
but I'd want to ideally cache a whole bunch of things here, docker images, crates, ccache, etc
that's in theory where a CDN would help though since those typically have far cheaper egress costs

ah so you're imagining the whole cache tarball (or equivalent) as one file in a bucket -- I was thinking each SMT query hits a different key so we effectively get merge/union semantics for free (versus "which version of the cache bundle do I take")
that's true yeah, I don't really mind so long as it works heh
and doesn't costs someone dollars-per-run
I'll play with this a bit
I can see if we can sort something out, but wouldn't want to get anyone's hopes up. And maybe @Tyler McMullen could get something working with Fastly?

Well, things escalated with the robots and I have an S3-backed SMT query cache now. Little LSM-tree-like cache (base packfile, delta of new query results, compaction after 10 deltas, read/write on main and readonly on PR branches); works locally on my own S3 bucket. 3MB download from S3 per CI run in 1..10 GETs (.0004/1k GETs, so cheap). No GC, grows forever, we can do a separate GC pass later if we want but 3MB is tiny

Is there a way to add my own role-limited IAM token on my personal AWS account to BA's secrets so I can test it in a PR? I'm willing to subsidize for a bit too if it takes time to fight the grues
IIRC what we did in rust-lang/rust was to expire everything after a month or so of inactivity so s3 sort of takes care of the GC for us
Ah, that's a good idea
or basically I think there's some option per-bucket to do that
that sounds great! And you should be able to add the secret to the repo with your access rights
cool, I will dig around
although for testing I'd recommend running in your personal fork if you can
not the full matrix of course but subsets

https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/pull/15083 -- I went ahead and just put the secrets in the repo and am testing here so I don't burn my own minutes / go through the trouble of testing on my fork
("secrets in the repo" meaning in secrets management under an environment visible from CI)
napkin math is ~$0.0001/month of storage (5MiB steady-state), a fraction of a cent per day in PUT/GET reqs, and maybe $4-5/month in egress for 100 CI jobs/day (note that job is gated on ISLE changes)
OK, that run worked -- merging this and jumping it to head of queue should fix our CI delays today
To be clear with current state: I'm happy to see that merged as-is, if r+'d, and let it use my bucket for now until folks figure out how to create one that's billed to BA
